cold_open.hook: Victoria's Secret jumped 40% yesterday. Yes. THAT Victoria's Secret. We're going to explain how a company America spent a decade roasting became the market's favorite comeback story.

markets.macro_note: Breadth paradox warning: S&P on a 9-day win streak but fewer stocks participating—classic late-cycle distribution pattern.

big_story.story_title: Victoria's Secret shares spike 40% after big earnings beat, raised sales outlook
big_story.angle: A brand that became a cultural punchline for toxic marketing and outdated sizing just proved Wall Street's death-knell predictions wrong—what actually changed, and is this a real turnaround or a one-quarter relief rally?

quick_hits.angle: Palo Alto Networks upgraded after earnings as cybersecurity becomes non-negotiable infrastructure, not a discretionary spend—the 'AI will kill us all' narrative finally hitting a wall.
Ulta Beauty also beat and raised—beauty retail is having a moment while big tech stumbles; margin expansion in a category that was supposed to be Amazon-proof.
Microsoft Build 2026 announcements: the company is throwing everything at AI integration, but the market just sold $18B in MSFT stock—investors voting 'we've heard this before.'
Fed Chair Warsh hiring a Project 2025 author signals the central bank is about to become a lot more political—regulatory theater meets actual policy.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Sailors trapped in the Strait of Hormuz for months are stressed and exhausted—turns out being a human cargo container in a geopolitical hostage situation is bad for morale; who knew.

yesterday_callback.topic: Victoria's Secret jumped 40% yesterday—turns out the internet's favorite punching bag figured out how to actually sell
yesterday_callback.fresh_take: Today we dig into whether this is a structural fix (new leadership, actual product strategy) or just a relief bounce that'll fade when the next earnings miss hits.

sign_off.callback_target: Victoria's Secret—because if a company can survive being the internet's favorite joke and still post a 40% day, maybe we're all underestimating comebacks.
